text: did you have another format in mind, i have to think there is even better but idk. or even further compression of that alone, and more so what about where the majority of it is already pre-defined data from the host for the map, since my approach assumes its all in the one mapfile
resolution: Answered the format-alternatives question and the user's pre-defined-host-data insight (no code). Ruled-in their point as the dominant win: the mapfile should store REFERENCES into platform registries (GEOMETRIES, materials, kinds, thingymajiggers, shaders) via a string-table lump + small-int index grids, embedding only map-authored content in a pakfile-style lump — the GoldSrc WAD-reference / Source VPK+pakfile precedent; the reference list doubles as a dependency manifest for load-time validation. On 'even better than RLE': surveyed palette+bitpack+RLE vs LZ4 vs zstd; concluded no codec beats restructuring — order of wins is reference-not-embed (100x+), default-value sparse chunks, palette indexing, then RLE mopping up; zstd would trade 10x decode speed for scraps. Added the principle: compress for transport (whole-blob lz4/zstd at distribution), lay out for runtime (RLE/raw mmap-able) — never bake general compression inside the format. One-mapfile shape preserved.
